stem: Why is the current acellular vaccine for \textit{Bordetella pertussis} (whooping cough) insufficient for achieving full herd immunity in the community?

options.text: It only protects against the catarrhal phase of the illness.
It does not reduce mucosal carriage of the bacteria.
It is a live vaccine that can cause mild infections in the elderly.
The immunity provided by the vaccine is lifelong after one dose.

explanation: Because the bacteria can still live in the throat of a vaccinated person, they can unknowingly transmit it to vulnerable individuals.
rationale: Consider the difference between a person being sick themselves versus being able to pass the germs to others.

optionExplanations.A: The vaccine effectively prevents the severe clinical symptoms of the disease across its phases but has a different limitation regarding transmission.
optionExplanations.B: Because the bacteria can still live in the throat of a vaccinated person, they can unknowingly transmit it to vulnerable individuals.
optionExplanations.C: The pertussis vaccine used in Australia is acellular (inactivated), not a live attenuated vaccine.
optionExplanations.D: Vaccine-induced immunity to pertussis actually wanes over time, which is why boosters and maternal immunization are necessary.

source.hint: Consider the difference between a person being sick themselves versus being able to pass the germs to others.
